gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the P2S's chamber ceiling. It has no chamber heater: its only heat is the bed, held in by a motorized airflow flap that switches to recirculation, which tops out at about 50 °C. The QIDI Q2 adds a separate 280 W PTC chamber heater (rated 350 W + 280 W) that holds up to 65 °C whatever the bed is doing.
standout_why: I compared against firstlayerlab.com/enclosed-3d-printers (cited), 3dprintgearlab.com/best/corexy-3d-printer (cited), layerwalker.com/3d-printer-enclosed and findmy3dprinter.com/buying-guides/enclosed-3d-printer. Popular Mechanics, also cited, blocked fetching. Firstlayerlab already explains passive (bed-heated) vs active chambers, gives the Q2's 65 °C, says the P1S chamber 'cannot be precisely controlled' and notes the P2S draws cool air from outside for PLA. It also covers opening the lid for PLA and filtration. Layerwalker gives a generic 'about 35 to 45 °C' for passive chambers. 3dprintgearlab only says 'no active heating listed' for the P2S. findmy3dprinter gives no chamber temperature in °C. None of them gives a P2S chamber ceiling (about 50 °C) or how its recirculation flap works. None gives the Q2 heater's 280 W figure or that it heats independently of the bed. The core passive-vs-active point is already on the cited rival, so this only adds detail.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's split. If the shopper mostly prints PLA, PETG or small ABS/ASA parts, the P2S works: its bed heat, held in by the flap, reaches about 50 °C, and in cooling mode it pulls in outside air so PLA can print with the door shut. If they print large ABS/ASA parts, PC or nylon, they need a heater that works independently of the bed, and among the cards shown only the QIDI Q2 has one (65 °C, 280 W PTC). The P1S, K1C and Adventurer 5M Pro all rely on bed heat alone. The Q2 heater pushes the rated draw to 630 W, which does not affect a standard 15 A US outlet. For a PLA-only buyer the Q2's heater is no advantage. QIDI's own blog lists heat creep among the risks of too much chamber heat.
